added_lines: or by calling (048) 79386259. “november remember ” pastoral initiative with the grim statistic of there having been 150 people killed on the country’s roads so far this year (12 more than the same period last year) – 45 of these people aged under 25 and 30 aged over 65 (of the 29 pedestri- ans killed, 10 were over 65) – we need to redouble our efforts as road users to do what we can to make our roads safer, especially as we enter the darker and colder months. to this end, while november is a time when we re- member our dead, this year, in an attempt to acknowl- edge that the life and death of each of us has its influ- ence on others, we would like as many people as possi- ble to take on a pledge to use the roads with care in november. the details of that pledge are to be found on posters and our social media pages. also, next weekend, people are asked to collect a prayer card for their car to be recited each day during the month and a bottle of holy water to be sprinkled on their car and kept there. chief superintendent goretti sheridan will address the cockhill novena on sunday 1 november and launch this initiative. there will be signage placed on the roads entering our two parishes to remind us of this. please do your best to participate in this and support i t. father bradley bank holiday the parish office will be closed on mon 26 oct and re-open at 9am on tuesday 27. annual mass for the dead the annual parish mass for the dead will take place on friday 27 november at 7pm in st mary’s, cockhill. families who have been bereaved from mid- october 2025 –31 october 2026 will be con- tacted in the next few weeks, but there will be an opportunity on the night for any family to bring forward a candle for someone who has died. candles will be on sale in the porch of the church on the night for €5. all welcome. buncrana

gospel reflection (matthew 22:34-40 ) in today’s gospel, jesus teaches that the greatest co mmandment is to love god wholeheartedly and to love our neighbour as ourselves.
these two responsibilities are inseparable and form the foundation of christian life.
loving god involves more than religious practices suc h as prayer, worship, and scripture reading.
it means trusting him in difficult times, remaining faithful through challenges, choosing what is right, and allowing him to guide every aspect of our lives.
genuine love for god is shown not only in words but also in daily actions.
our love for god becomes visible in how we treat others.
we cannot truly love god while harming, judging, or refusing to forgive those around us.
instead, we are called to show compassion, kindness, patience, and mercy.
even simple acts such as listening, encouraging, forgiving, and helping those in need can become powerful expressions of god's love.
jesus also calls us to recognize the dignity and wort h of every person, including those who differ from us or disappoint us.
true love does not ignore wrongdoing, but it speaks the truth with respect and sets boundaries wit hout hatred.
the central message of this gospel is that love must be at the heart of both our relationship with god and our relationship with othe rs.
faith is not measured by religious knowledge or activities alone, but by wheth er it transforms us into more loving people.
when love guides our thoughts, words , and actions, our lives become a living witness to god's presence in the world.
may the lord bless us with hearts open to love.
may us to see christ in one another and to bring kindness, hope, and compassion wherever we go.
